title: Research Day
intro: Sixty posters on easels fill the atrium, from second-year projects to the residents' trials. Judges with clipboards drift between them. You have a program and two free hours.

steps.say: "Pick three posters and ask each presenter one real question. That's how you'll find a mentor for the summer."
steps.speaker: Dr. Lena Park, Associate Dean for Student Affairs

steps.say: Poster 14: "A community walking program for blood pressure: a randomized trial." A fourth-year talks you through it.

steps.question: res_ci_01
steps.lead: "What do you make of our result?"

steps.say: Poster 22 is an observational study using a health survey of forty thousand adults.

steps.question: res_confounding_01
steps.lead: The presenter grins. "The judges asked the same thing. Your answer?"

steps.say: Poster 31: a resident's analysis of a stroke-prevention trial.

steps.question: res_nnt_01
steps.lead: "Everyone quotes the relative risk. What's the number that matters to a patient?"

steps.question: res_sensitivity_01
steps.lead: At the next poster, about a new blood test:

choice.prompt: A second-year asks you to mind her poster while she runs to the restroom. A judge arrives and asks a question you can't answer.

options.text: "I'm not the author and I don't know, but here's what I understand of the methods. She'll be back in a minute and can answer properly."
options.reply: The judge smiles and makes a note. The second-year comes back and answers it well.

options.text: Make up something that sounds plausible.
options.reply: The judge frowns at the poster, then at you. It was wrong.

options.text: Say nothing and wait for her to come back.
options.reply: The judge moves on to the next poster.

choice.lesson: Say what you don't know; never bluff about data

steps.say: Dr. Park stops you by the coffee urn. "A few of the faculty take first-years for summer research. I'll send you the list."

feedback: You leave with three business cards and an invitation to a lab meeting.
A good morning: two of the posters make you want to start a project.
Biostatistics is a skill like any other. The library has a good introductory text on the reserve shelf.
